### Global Metadata
A complete 100-second lively Japanese summer-festival (natsumatsuri) evening piece for a courtyard full of lantern-lit food stalls, festive and joyful matsuri-bayashi feeling. 118 BPM, G major. A bright bamboo shinobue flute melody, taiko drums with a lively matsuri rhythm, a small kane hand gong, shamisen strumming, hand clapping, supported by warm strings and a light modern acoustic bass. Pure instrumental ensemble piece.

### Vocal Details
None. Instrumental only: the shinobue flute and shamisen carry the festive melody; drums keep the matsuri rhythm.

### Timed Arrangement
0-14 seconds: taiko and kane gong kick off the festival rhythm. 14-46 seconds: the shinobue flute plays a festive melody over shamisen and drums. 46-74 seconds: shamisen solo with hand claps, strings lift the harmony. 74-100 seconds: flute and full ensemble return with the main tune, energetic but not loud. Keep tempo, texture and loudness consistent from start to end; no big climax. The piece must play for the full 100 seconds and must not end early, ending cleanly on the tonic so it can loop.
